sections.normalized_html:
We are given the volume of the cone and its height. The formula for the volume of a cone is [MATH: V = \dfrac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h.]

Now, we substitute [MATH: V = \dfrac{5}{4}\pi] and [MATH: h = 2] into the formula and simplify: [MATH: (5)/(4)π|= (1)/(3)πr^{2}(2); (5)/(4)π|= (2)/(3)πr^{2}; (5)/(4)|= (2)/(3)r^{2}; (15)/(8)|= r^{2}; r|= sqrt((15)/(8))]

Finally, we rationalize the denominator: [MATH: r|= sqrt((15)/(8)); r|= (sqrt(15))/(2sqrt(2)) ⋅ (sqrt(2))/(sqrt(2)); r|= (sqrt(30))/(4)]

So, the radius of the base is [MATH: \dfrac{\sqrt{30}}{4}] meters.

items.title: Finding the Height of a Cone Given Its Volume and Base Area

sections.normalized_html: A right circular cone has a volume of [MATH: 19{,}200\pi] cubic inches, and the area of its base is [MATH: 1{,}200\pi] square inches. What is the slant height, in inches, of this cone?
sections.readable_text: A right circular cone has a volume of [MATH: 19{,}200\pi] cubic inches, and the area of its base is [MATH: 1{,}200\pi] square inches. What is the slant height, in inches, of this cone?

sections.normalized_html:
We are given the volume and the base area of the cone and are asked to find the slant height. To do this, we first need to determine the height [MATH: h] and the radius [MATH: r,] and then use the Pythagorean Theorem.

The volume formula for a cone is [MATH: V = \dfrac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h.]

Since the area of the base is [MATH: 1,200\pi,] we know that [MATH: \pi r^2 = 1{,}200\pi.]

We substitute this into the volume formula and simplify: [MATH: V|= (1)/(3) ⋅ πr^{2} ⋅ h; 19, 200π|= (1)/(3) ⋅ 1,200π ⋅ h; 19, 200|= 400 ⋅ h; 48|= h; h|= 48]

Now, we solve for the slant height using the Pythagorean Theorem [MATH: l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2}.]

We already know that [MATH: \pi r^2 = 1{,}200\pi], so [MATH: r^2 = 1{,}200.]

Substituting into the formula: [MATH: l|= sqrt(r^{2} + h^{2}); = sqrt(1,200 + 48^{2}); = sqrt(1,200 + 2,304); = sqrt(3,504); ≈ 59.19] rounded to [MATH: 2] decimal places.

So, the slant height is [MATH: 59.19] inches.
